item.title: 24 Jump Street, the long-awaited next installment in the Jonah Hill and Channing Tatum buddy cop franchise, finally has a release date.
item.description:
24 Jump Street, the long-awaited next installment in the Jonah Hill and Channing Tatum buddy cop franchise, finally has a release date.
Sony has confirmed that 24 Jump Street will release on December 10, 2027, with Tatum, Hill, and Ice Cube all returning. The film was officially announced earlier this year after years of hopes from fans. Despite its title, it is actually the third film; there was supposed to be a third film in the 2010s which would've linked the Jump Street crew with the Men in Black, but plans for the project fell apart.
Given the extended gap between films, some thought the franchise fizzled out. However, Jonah Hill and Meghan Malloy penned a script for a new movie, which will be helmed by Rodney Rothman (Spider-Man: Into the Spider-Verse). It's unclear who else will star in the project or what it will be about, but given the major gap between these movies, it seems likely that the duo won't be able to integrate back into a high school or college. The first two films already made self-aware jokes about the two looking much older than the people they were supposed to be portraying undercover, so it's possible they could just continue to lean into that.
With a release next holiday season, it seems likely that shooting will begin imminently in order to hit its launch date. As a result, we may be able to expect some additional casting news any day. It's another win for those who are seeking raunchy R-rated comedies on the big screen, and hopefully, the film succeeds and can send a message to other studios that there's an appetite for other projects like it. Currently, it'll open around the same time as Avengers: Secret Wars, so it may have steep competition unless Marvel pushes that film back.
Cade Onder is a freelancer for IGN's news team. He covers all things entertainment, including gaming, film, and more. You can find him on Twitter @Cade_Onder.

item.title: Reacher star Alan Ritchson has been confirmed to play one of the titular Helldivers in the game’s film adaptation, which is now set to release in 2028.
item.description:
Reacher star Alan Ritchson has been confirmed to play one of the titular Helldivers in the hit game’s film adaptation, which is now set to release in 2028.
As told by Sony Pictures in a September 30 press release, Helldivers’ release date has been shifted from November 10, 2027 to June 9, 2028.
Justin Lin, best known for helming several of the Fast & Furious movies, is still set to direct, with Hutch Parker, PlayStation Productions’ Asad Qizilbash, and Justin Lin’s Perfect Storm Entertainment producing the film.
As described by Sony Pictures, Helldivers’ story centers on an “elite unit of soldiers — known as Helldivers — who must battle alien creatures threatening to destroy the fictional planet of Super Earth.” Ritchson will star as “one of the Helldivers,” though it remains to be seen if he is the movie’s main character or not.
Ritchson was already rumored to be involved in the Helldivers adaptation; a report from Deadline earlier this month stated the six-foot-three action hero was in talks to star. Now that this has been confirmed, we can't think of anyone better to join the Helldivers' ranks and help spread sweet, sweet Democracy through the galaxy, especially given his standout performance in Prime Video's Reacher.
The movie could have looked drastically different, and it almost did; Jason Momoa (Game of Thrones, Supergirl) was initially slated to star in Helldivers, but left the project sometime this summer for unknown reasons.
First announced in January 2025, the Helldivers movie was received with mixed reactions from fans, especially after they learned that director Justin Lin is not a gamer. The Hollywood Reporter described this as a "strength" for Lin, saying he "leaned into it" when pitching his idea for the project.
Unsurprisingly, this caused an uproar among players... but the CEO of Arrowhead, the developer of Helldivers 2, assured them that he "trusts" Lin with the IP.
"We are not Hollywood people, and we don't know what it takes to make a movie. And therefore we don't, and shouldn't, have final say," he said, urging fans to "let him work his magic."
We're hopeful that Lin's Helldivers will be just as fantastic of a love letter to the game as Zach Cregger's Resident Evil was to Capcom's flagship horror series. It's a good time for video game adaptations overall, and more are on the horizon, with Legendary's Street Fighter set to hit theaters on October 16.
Image Credit: Dimitrios Kambouris/Getty Images

item.title: Crimson Desert's first expansion was only just announced at the State of Play in September with a very ambitious October 15 release date. Unfortunately it seems that target was a little too ambitious.
item.description:
Crimson Desert's first expansion was only just announced at the State of Play in September with a very ambitious October 15 release date. Unfortunately, it seems that target was a little too ambitious.
Pearl Abyss announced that the Charting the Unknown expansion would be delayed by two weeks, in order to "deliver a more polished and stable gameplay experience." But even with this delay, the new expansion is coming remarkably close to the game's initial release, and hopefully the developer will have even more content planned for the future.
The expansion comes just seven months after Crimson Desert intially released back on March 19. And while the reception to the game was mixed, a lot of its initial issues have since been ironed out, turning the game into one of the breakout hits of the year.
Hello, Greymanes. We would like to share an update regarding Crimson Desert’s upcoming DLC. pic.twitter.com/mKNmYn10jX
This first expansion will expand the game to a new zone, and will bring sea exploration to the already expansive world. Charting the unknown will also bring more robust base building, with the trailer suggesting you'll be able to actually build new buildings, which will only add another hundred hours to my play time.
Crimson Desert's Charting the Unknown expansion will now launch on October 29, and will set you back $24.99. And just like the base game, it'll be available on PlayStation 5, Xbox Series X and PC.

item.title: A modder who was porting GTA 5 to Nintendo Switch taunted Rockstar Games and was immediately hit with a cease and desist.
item.description:
A modder who was porting GTA 5 to Nintendo Switch taunted Rockstar Games and was immediately hit with a cease and desist.
The modder, known as Mojso, was planning to bring GTA 5 and GTA Online to Nintendo Switch for modded versions of the console and got a bit cocky. After Rockstar Games recently posted its guidelines for modding (which forbids unofficial ports), the modder posted: "Try me Rockstar, [I don't give a f**k.]"
Three days later, the modder's Discord server was taken down for copyright infringement, but it didn't seem to deter them. After many warned them about how litigous Rockstar Games and parent company Take-Two are, the modder suggested they aren't worried about it: "Copyright infringement is anything but enforced in Serbia."
Less than a week later, the modder confirmed they had received a cease and desist from Take-Two Interactive and thanked the company for its "mercy." As a result, the port will never see the light of day, as Mojso has stated that they don't want to risk any legal issues.
"Paralympics Productions is shutting down on October 3rd. Thank you everyone who supported us through tough times and lenghty development. I am sorry for not fulfilling your expectations and leaving you high and dry. I am thankful for Take-Two's mercy so this is the definitive end," they wrote.
When people pointed back to the modder's post about taunting Rockstar, Mojso noted that they didn't actually expect Rockstar to do anything.
"They tried me," Mojso said. "[What the] f**k [do] you want me to do? Fight with them in court? I wasn't expecting them to hit back hard."
The modder had been working on this port using leaked GTA 5 source code, which has resulted in a bevy of other leaks and issues. Ultimately, it's probably in your best interest to not taunt massive corporations that are known for hunting down people that mess with their IP.
Cade Onder is a freelancer for IGN's news team. He covers all things entertainment, including gaming, film, and more. You can find him on Twitter @Cade_Onder.

item.title: A new report claims that a brand new Uncharted game featuring Nathan Drake is one of several projects in the works at Naughty Dog.
item.description:
A new report claims that a brand new Uncharted game featuring Nathan Drake is one of several projects in the works at Naughty Dog.
MP1st has reported that the next Uncharted game, which is not a remake of any kind, is in active development at Naughty Dog. The game will feature Nathan Drake in some capacity, but it's unclear if he's the lead, in a supporting role, or even just a cameo. The project is being helmed by Shaun Escayag, who previously led Uncharted: The Lost Legacy, a standalone expansion for Uncharted 4. This has been heavily speculated for years now, with Escayag having recently teased the project himself on his socials.
The director was in Trindad earlier this year for "research" and posted a picture of a very old-looking cannon. MP1st noted that the new Uncharted game is set to be Naughty Dog's next game following the release of Intergalactic, which is speculated to launch next year. The studio recently confirmed that it will give a proper look at its upcoming sci-fi game in 2027, as well.
Additionally, Naughty Dog confirmed it has multiple Last of Us projects in the works beyond the existing HBO TV series. Series creator Neil Druckmann has avoided revealing what mediums these projects will utilize, so they could be shows, films, books, or games. However, it feels like a safe bet that at least one of them is probably a video game, and fans are hoping it's The Last of Us Part 3.
The next Uncharted game is expected to be at least a couple of years away. Uncharted 4 was released a decade ago and put a nice bow on Nathan Drake's adventures. However, given that he remained alive and well, the door has always been left open for another escapade. Now, Drake could be joined by his daughter, Cassie, who takes a clear interest in Nathan's same hobbies.
Cade Onder is a freelancer for IGN's news team. He covers all things entertainment, including gaming, film, and more. You can find him on Twitter @Cade_Onder.

item.title: Ordering food through DoorDash is probably one of the biggest examples of how modern life has grown incredibly convenient, but apparently, there are still some people who think scrolling through an app is too much work. Now, you'll be able to just text DoorDash and have it order food for you without needing to figure out what, exactly, you feel like eating.
item.description:
Ordering food through DoorDash is probably one of the biggest examples of how modern life has grown incredibly convenient, but apparently, there are still some people who think scrolling through an app is too much work. Now, you'll be able to just text DoorDash and have it order food for you without needing to figure out what, exactly, you feel like eating.
DoorDash announced the feature earlier this week, and the idea is that you'll text an AI agent through iMessages – apparently Android support will come sometime in the future – an idea of what you want for dinner. Then, DoorDash's AI agent will browse through all the restaurants in your area and give you suggestions based on your past orders and what you included in your text.
One of the examples DoorDash includes is asking its bot for your usual Friday night order, and it'll remember what you usually get, along with any modifications you usually make. This is already pretty easy to do within the app, which usually has your last few orders at the top of the screen anyways. Ironically, texting a robot for your usual order might end up having more button presses than just opening the app and ordering normally.
In some ways, this actually feels like a blast from the past. SMS ordering used to be a thing, before the rise of smartphones. Dominoes introduced a way to order pizza by sending them an emoji all the way back in 2015, according to TechTimes. Though, to be fair, that was just one restaurant.
If you want to cut scrolling through an app out of your DoorDash routine, you can sign up to test this feature on DoorDash's website, but only if you're on iOS. Android users will just have to order food the new-old-fashioned way for a while longer. It's not clear when this feature will leave beta, but either way, it seems like ordering food will get even easier, regardless of whether or not it actually needed to.

item.title: The European Commission is taking action against nine video game companies over their digital currency and pricing of in-game items with the goal of protecting players’ rights.
item.description:
The European Commission is taking action against nine video game companies over their digital currency and pricing of in-game items with the goal of protecting players’ rights.
Launched on September 29, 2026, these actions are a follow-up to the Consumer Protection Cooperation Network’s Key Principles on in-game virtual currencies, which are a set of guidelines released in March 2025 that “promote transparency and fairness” for in-game currency and transactions.
These Key Principles guidelines were reached after the CPC Network had extensive discussions with game studios and publishers — but despite these talks, it found indications that a “high number of video game companies” hadn’t made any substantive changes to their games as a result of its public guidance, “nor as a result of the extensive talks between the CPC Network and the gaming industry that have taken place over the course of the past years.”
The CPC Network name-dropped these companies in a joint statement with the European Commission on September 30, publicly asking that they bring their in-game currency and transaction systems in line with their guidelines. These companies include Activision Blizzard UK, Mojang AB, Riot Games Limited, Supercell Oy, and Ubisoft EMEA SAS.
“Some video games directly exhort children to make purchases, despite an explicit prohibition in EU consumer protection law. Consumers across Europe should be able to play and interact with video games without being tricked into spending more money or time on video games than they want,” the CPC Network’s joint statement reads.
As outlined by the European Commission, its newest actions focus on seven core principles: providing clear and transparent pricing, not obscuring costs, not forcing unwanted currency purchases, providing clear information before the purchase, respecting the right to withdraw, using fair and understandable terms, and protecting vulnerable consumers.
The European Commission says that games must now show the actual, real-world price of in-game items that players are able to buy using virtual currency. Additionally, games must not require players to jump through hoops with currency exchanges or use multiple currencies, which would make the actual cost of these items unclear.
On top of that, games must not make players “feel obliged to buy an excessive amount of virtual currencies to progress or enjoy the game,” and they should be allowed to withdraw from any contracts within a two-week period, including for “unused virtual currency.”
“Roughly half of Europeans play video games, making gaming a major part of our digital economy and everyday lives,” Michael McGrath, Commissioner for Democracy, Justice, the Rule of Law and Consumer Protection, said in a statement.
“With that reach comes responsibility. The industry must ensure that its games do not expose players — especially children — to harmful or unfair practices. The game must be fair, and the rules must be respected. National authorities, with the support of the Commission, will make sure they are enforced.”
This is the latest big swing from the EU in the video game space after documents outlining the The EU Kids Act was shared online. This proposed legislation would require age verification for several online services, including certain multiplayer games that are “risky to minors.”

item.title: Wizards of the Coast trots out a new MTG Secret Lair on a monthly basis at this point, and while crossovers aren't anything new, the new 'super drop' brings Jim Henson's Labyrinth and KPop Demon Hunters to the card game for the first time.
item.description:
Wizards of the Coast trots out a new MTG Secret Lair on a monthly basis at this point, and while crossovers aren't anything new for the franchise, this new 'superdrop' brings Jim Henson's Labyrinth and KPop Demon Hunters to the card game for the first time.
Wizards of the Coast has just announced the Corn Maze Superdrop, clearly in time for Halloween, but instead of going with a darker horror twist like it did with the Junji Ito drop, all of these collections are relatively lighthearted. Of course, for most people, the biggest draws will be the KPop Demon Hunters and Labyrinth drops – the latter of which has three collections – along with a Marvel Zombies collection.
The three Labyrinth drops are the highlight of the Corn Maze Superdrop, though. The Secret Lair x Jim Henson's Labyrinth Fear Me, Love Me drop is entirely focused on Goblin kindred cards, and is headlined by Muxus, Goblin Grandee, a Goblin Staple, posing as Jareth, Goblin King with a beautiful illustration of David Bowie. Of course, there's also a copy of Claim the Firstborn as The Kidnapping of Toby. For some reason, though, this drop also has a copy of Trinisphere, which doesn't really fit into any conceivable goblin deck, but at least it has some cool art of Bowie holding a bunch of orbs.
It wouldn't be a Secret Lair Superdrop without some nigh-unreadable cards, and that's where the Secret Lair x Jim Henson's Labyrinth: Through the Labyrinth comes in. The art on these cards are all gorgeous, though I could totally see some of them being hard to parse from across the table. Still, Wizards decided to print Leveler in this drop, which you can combine with The Beamtown Bullies or Thassa's Oracle to make your pod wish they were dropped in the Labyrinth.
There's also a KPop Demon Hunters drop, which has some incredible cards with combo potential. This one comes with a copy of Freed From The Real and Underworld Breach, both of which will be notorious in decks that are built around them. There's a reason Breach has been banned in multiple formats, after all.
And Wizards is still trying to work more Marvel content into Magic, this time with a Marvel Zombies drop that's focused on Zombie kindred cards. But, as cool as it would be to have a commander deck helmed by Zombie Thor or Zombie Scarlet witch, none of the cards in this drop are really worth the high price you'd be paying for them, unless you really love Marvel Zombies.
Some of the other drops are seriously cool, too. The Manufactured Grounds by See Machine drop brings some incredible art to the original artifact land cycle from Mirrodin. That drop probably doesn't make a lot of sense from a purely financial perspective, but damn, does it look cool. Then there's the Peace, Love and Treefolk drop, which gives Timber Protector its first meaningful reprint besides the Lord of the Rings commander decks.
I'm probably going to pick up all of the Labyrinth drops, and if you want to grab one (or all) of them too, the Corn Maze Superdrop will be available starting at 9am PT / 12pm ET on October 12. Wizards of the Coast will even toss in a Labyrinth-flavored copy of Maze of Ith on any order over $199.

item.title: Emmy-nominated actor Vincent D’Onofrio has somehow found himself at war with a self-proclaimed ‘gooner’ over Deborah Ann Woll’s appearance in God of War Laufey.
item.description:
Emmy-nominated actor Vincent D’Onofrio has somehow found himself at war with a self-proclaimed ‘gooner’ over Deborah Ann Woll’s appearance in God of War Laufey.
The next game in the God of War series is fast approaching, this time following the adventures of Laufey, Kratos’ second wife and Loki’s mother in Norse mythology.
Given the current state of social media, it’s almost unsurprising that this fact alone has riled up the online rage machine — but it seems the controversy has grown so loud that other A-List actors are taking notice.
More recently, the conversation has shifted from Deborah Ann Woll’s in-game appearance as Laufey to her special armor sets within the upcoming game. As told by a Twitter/X user who goes by the name ‘Geralt of Goonia,' Sony’s Santa Monica Studio “would rather go bankrupt than give you an ounce of female attractiveness,” specifically when it comes to how much skin these armor sets cover.
Unexpectedly, Vincent D’Onofrio — who acted alongside Woll in Netflix and Marvel’s Daredevil series — chimed into the conversation to defend his co-star and proclaim his excitement to play the game alongside his son when it releases this coming February.
“Not that you asked, but… In no way do I agree with you,” he wrote. “Deborah is beautiful and extremely talented. She is as smart as a whip and a complete nerd. Also incredibly kind. How perfect she is! And a good friend. I am a fan of God of War. I, for one, cannot wait to play the new game with my son.”
Not that you asked, but...In no way do i agree with you. Deborah is beautiful and extremely talented. She is as smart as whip and a complete nerd. Also incredibly kind.How perfect she is! And a good friend. I am a fan of God of War. I for one cannot wait to play the new…
Despite getting owned by Kingpin himself, Geralt of Goonia continued his tirade, leading to no end of humorous responses and memes from players defending Laufey and agreeing with D’Onofrio’s excitement about playing the game.
Laufey has been at the center of a few discussions between notable folks in the gaming and entertainment space lately; the original creator of God of War, David Jaffe, called the game “stupid” during a recent live stream, and accused its creative director, Ariel Lawrence, of having a “lack of passion” for the title itself. (He later clarified these remarks in a tweet and defended Lawrence from the ensuing harassment campaign that started against her as a result of his comments.)
Prior to that, The Last of Us director Bruce Straley used Laufey as an example of AAA games that failed to “excite” him, though he similarly clarified this statement and apologized for bringing "uninvited and unnecessary negative attention” to the title.
Woll, for her part, hasn’t let the negativity get her down. Speaking with a fan at Florida Supercon in July, she said she’s confident that Laufey is a fantastic game, which has, at least in part, helped her avoid being affected by the backlash from trolls online.
"Genuinely, I thought I was going to be much more offended by it, but one, I'm not on social media, so that helps, and two, I don't know, I feel totally unbothered," Woll said. "Because I just know it's great. It's okay if it's not your cup of tea, but in no universe is it bad,” she said.
God of War Laufey releases on 16, 2027 exclusively on PlayStation 5.

item.title: Xbox CEO Asha Sharma has denied reports suggesting Microsoft was considering selling its gaming business.
item.description:
Xbox CEO Asha Sharma has denied reports suggesting Microsoft was considering selling its gaming business.
In an interview with the New York Times, Sharma declared: “Xbox is not for sale.”
“We will do whatever it takes to set the company up for success, and we will look at the right partnerships, the right operating model and everything needed to achieve that,” Sharma continued.
One of the big questions emerging from Sharma’s appointment as Xbox CEO earlier this year, and the subsequent layoffs and restructuring that have occurred in recent months, revolves around the long-term future of Microsoft’s gaming business. Will Microsoft sell off Xbox? Are the cuts and restructure laying the groundwork for a sale?
Details on a potential shakeup came from The Information (via Reuters), which said that Microsoft hadn't ruled out turning the Xbox brand into a wholly-owned subsidiary. It said the move could result in Xbox being operated as a joint venture with other partners or even potentially sold.
Sharma’s Xbox reset has since become clearer. Nearly 2,000 Xbox staff have already been cut, with more to come this financial year. Multiple studios have either exited Xbox or face closure, and various games have been canceled. Xbox is now focused on fewer, bigger video game franchises such as The Elder Scrolls, Fallout, and Minecraft, with the likes of Halo moved over to Call of Duty company Activision. Through it all, there are question marks hanging over the viability of Xbox’s confirmed next-gen console, Project Helix.
While some believe this reset and the cuts that have come with it are part of a strategy to make Xbox easier to sell, analysts aren’t convinced. Some have said Xbox would likely have few suitors interested in buying the business outright, considering Microsoft bought Activision Blizzard for an eye-watering $69 billion, Xbox’s huge payroll, extensive studio setup, and hardware business. More likely, analysts have suggested, is that big companies may pick off parts of Xbox as Microsoft continues to look to trim the business.
The NYT speculates that an eventual spinoff could create an independent Xbox that would partner with Microsoft while keeping its costs off the company’s balance sheet. But Sharma cast doubt on this as an option, too, saying: “We’ve got a long way to go with Microsoft, and we’re going to take the long-term view.”
Who would even buy Xbox when Xbox itself admits its business is unhealthy? Xbox ended the financial year with a 3% accountability margin (assumed to be profit margin), down year-over-year. Excluding Activision Blizzard King, over the past five years Microsoft spent over $20 billion on ongoing investments in what Sharma called its content, platform, and hardware “subsidy,” but annual revenue declined nearly half a billion during that time.
“We are operating at margins that are 3-10x lower than comparable platform and publishing businesses,” Sharma said in a blog post announcing the layoffs in July. “We entered Gen 9 with a smaller install base and a higher cost structure. To grow, we bet on Game Pass, multi-platform, and a broader portfolio of content. While those businesses have created meaningful value, they did not grow at the pace we expected. As that happened, our core business weakened, and we added more teams, more investment, and more time, hoping for a better outcome. And now the industry is facing the most severe hardware crisis in its history. We must reset Xbox.”
Meanwhile, Microsoft has increased the price of Xbox consoles. Microsoft blamed this on console storage and memory prices, which have increased by more than 2.5x, and it expects another doubling by the fall of 2027. "The entire consumer electronics industry is struggling with the current components crisis, but the effects are particularly hard on consoles," Microsoft said when it announced the price rises. "... the industry is facing the most severe hardware crisis in its history," Sharma added in the Xbox "Reset" memo.
For now, Sharma’s focus is on growing Xbox, which, she told the NYT, still has 500 million players a month. Microsoft's ambitious target is for Xbox to reach 1 billion people a day — a figure that has been ridiculed online. How will Xbox achieve this? By tapping into markets such as Africa and South Asia via cloud computing, and investing in Minecraft as a Roblox competitor, the NYT reported.

item.title: Capcom has a plan for when its rollout of Resident Evil remakes eventually catches up with newer games in the series, and considers Resident Evil 7 as a "turning point."
item.description:
Capcom has a plan for when its rollout of Resident Evil remakes eventually catches up with newer games in the series, and considers Resident Evil 7 as a "turning point."
That's according to Jun Takeuchi, a Capcom veteran who has served as excutive producer for the series over the past decade, who has acknowledged the fact that Capcom's hugely popular remakes are slowly running out of classic games to re-release. The publisher has already remade Resident Evil 2, 3 and 4 to great success, with a new version of Code Veronica slated for next year.
It has previously been reported that a Resident Evil 0 remake will follow in 2028, and that a Resident Evil 1 remake has also been considered. Of the mainline Resident Evil games, this would then just leave Resident Evil 5 and 6 as the only titles left to get new versions — both of which would be interesting prospects, for separate reasons.
While Capcom likely has enough remakes to keep their releases going for another decade, there will come a point where the publisher needs to decide whether to remake other titles, or start remaking its remakes all over again. Or... do something else, Takeuchi teased.
"The current Resident Evil series is being developed along two tracks," Takeuchi noted, writing in the just-released Biohazard 30th anniversary special magazine book now available in Japan (thanks, RENews_X, via The Gamer).
"Someday, the remake series will catch up with the era of the numbered titles, and we are already thinking about what we will do when that happens," he continued. "In fact, we have been gradually preparing for that since around Resident Evil Village. The appearance of names such as Umbrella and Spencer, as well as the return of Raccoon City in Requiem, are also in preparation for a 'crossover'.
"At first, we included these elements with the sense that they were fan service, but users were far more delighted by them than we had imagined, and they even began analysing the thoughts that the development team had privately kept to itself. So, as a series, we decided to respond to users' expectations and pushed this setup further in Village and Requiem."
Takeuchi went on to state that Capcom regarded Resident Evil 7 "as a turning point for the series" as it was in development when its plans to start remaking older games really came to fruition. Does this mean that everything before 7 is set to be remade one day, while 7 and onwards is considered too new?
Resident Evil 5 sold hugely well, with particular interest in the game in the wake of the top-rated Resident Evil 4. (Sadly, 5 was nowhere near as good.) But any new version of the game would see Capcom returning to the controversy over 5's African setting and companion character Sheva. As for Resident Evil 6, which featured a range of protagonists, it just isn't very good. But perhaps Capcom could salvage it in an eventual new version?
What's more interesting here is Capcom's suggestion that is using its remakes to seed ideas it will pick up again in newer titles, when that "crossover" point eventually happens. After all, Resident Evil has now been going for 30 years, which is a long time for anyone to remember plot details without being able to revisit early entries.
For now, though, all of that is a long time off — and there's plenty to look forward to. The promising-looking Resident Evil Veronica is next on the docket, and we've already asked Capcom some of our burning questions...
Tom Phillips is IGN's News Editor. You can reach Tom at tom_phillips@ign.com or find him on Bluesky @tomphillipseg.bsky.social

item.title: Microsoft’s high-profile deal for Hideo Kojima’s Physint is reportedly “substantially below what Xbox would typically spend to develop a premium game.”
item.description:
Microsoft’s high-profile deal for Hideo Kojima’s Physint is reportedly “substantially below what Xbox would typically spend to develop a premium game.”
Xbox snapped up Physint after Kojima pitched the game to new CEO Asha Sharma — a pitch Kojima conducted after Sony canceled the previously PlayStation-exclusive project. For more on that, check out IGN’s recent interview with Hideo Kojima himself, where he talks through how he found out Sony had ditched Physint, and his concern about the fate of Kojima Productions.
Since then, there have been a number of online reports about the budget for Physint, with some claiming the deal was around $400 million. Subsequent reports claimed the figure was substantially less. Now, in a New York Times profile of Sharma, it was reported that Xbox may have negotiated a deal for less than you’d expect for what is expected to be a full price, triple-A spiritual successor to Metal Gear Solid from the creator of the franchise.
Here’s the relevant blurb from the NYT article:
After hours of diplomatic conversation about her competitors, Sharma had a rare moment of speechlessness when discussing the deal for Kojima’s upcoming stealth game Physint. She laughed at the idea of apologizing to Sony before shrugging and saying she was happy Kojima chose to work with Xbox.
The agreement was substantially below what Xbox would typically spend to develop a premium game, according to people close to the agreement, and included film and TV rights. Sharma also clarified that work with Sony would continue: “Competition and collaboration can coexist.”
Xbox’s deal for Physint includes adaptations (Death Stranding is getting exactly that). Kojima told IGN that Microsoft was “not thinking of just funding a game. They're thinking about movies and anime. It's more about the IP. Let's create a new IP. And that's bigger in scale, so to speak. And not many other game publishers or game developers have that kind of vision.”
So, whatever the exact figure, we know Xbox is funding Physint the project, not just the video game. So we might see a Physint live-action movie (will it go up against the Metal Gear Solid movie?!), potentially an anime, and maybe even more.
Video game production budgets have risen dramatically in recent years, especially in the west where development costs have skyrocketed. Triple-A video game sales haven’t risen to match these rising costs, putting pressure on the triple-A video game industry.
In the wake of Physint’s move to Xbox, Bloomberg reported that Sony had concerns around the success of Death Stranding, as well as Physint’s development timeline, budget, and platform strategy. Kojima Productions issued a statement in response, although it failed to directly address Bloomberg’s reporting.
“Make no mistake, this was a serious situation for the studio with a range of potentially significant implications,” Kojima Productions said. “While we recognise that the article may have caused alarm, we want to reassure you all, for the record: that the studio is in a healthy, profitable state, development for Physint continues to move forward with Xbox, and our relationship with PlayStation remains strong.​”
Physint remains without a release window. It is expected after the launch of OD, Kojima's next video game for Xbox.
Wesley is Director, News at IGN. Find him on Twitter at @wyp100. You can reach Wesley at wesley_yinpoole@ign.com or confidentially at wyp100@proton.me.

item.title: October's PlayStation Plus monthly games lineup has been officially revealed by Sony.
item.description:
October's PlayStation Plus monthly games lineup has been officially revealed by Sony.
This month's trio of titles include a slightly out of date racer, a monster-filled extraction shooter, and a multiplayer voxel shooter. Let's dive in.
Launched last year, F1 25 is the actually pretty good entry in Codemasters' long-running Formula 1 racing series that we awarded with an 8/10. "F1 25 is a far broader and better package than last year’s installment, and it’s comfortably the strongest the series has been since the fan favourite F1 2020," we wrote in IGN's F1 25 review.
Next up, Hunt: Showdown 1896, Crytek's first-person extraction shooter that sends you off to fight mythological monsters. Originally launched in early acces back in 2018, when we awarded the game a 7.5/10 in our Hunt: Showdown 1896 review, this PS5 version also features a battle royale offering. And don't worry if you haven't played the first 1895 games in the series, you'll soon pick it up.
Finally, Earth Defense Force: World Brothers 2 is available for PS4 and PS5. This third-person shooter with local and online co-op tells the story of what happened to the voxelEarth after the events of the first installment. Brothers from across the world reunite to face an unprecedented threat brought about by an all-new enemy that threatens to tear the Earth apart all over again.
PlayStation Plus Extra/Premium:
So, anything you fancy?

item.title: Pirates of the Caribbean actor Geoffrey Rush has said he's keen to make a return to Disney's swashbuckling franchise, if only to "annoy Jack Sparrow" one last time.
item.description:
Pirates of the Caribbean actor Geoffrey Rush has said he's keen to make a return to Disney's swashbuckling franchise, if only to "annoy Jack Sparrow" one last time.
Rush is one of just three actors to appear in all five Pirates of the Caribbean movies, alongside Johnny Depp's Captain Jack Sparrow and Kevin McNally's loyal first mate Gibbs. And while we don't know yet which characters are set to return for Disney's long-awaited sixth blockbuster, all signs point to several classic characters being brought back.
Of course, Rush's character Hector Barbossa died in the finale of 2016's Pirates of the Caribbean: Dead Men Tell No Tales, the franchise's final film to date. But even this would not necessarily stop him from returning, Rush believes.
"There's been a big enough break," Rush told Entertainment Weekly, discussing his desire to return. "I said, you know, I sacrificed myself for my daughter, I don't want it to be too easy and too cheesy that I come back and go: 'give me another payday.' I respect the scale of the opera that's almost been created in that 20 year period.
"I liken it to... Shakespeare," Rush continued, "and Hamlet's father coming back as a ghost. I thought, that would take good writing but just to come back and annoy Jack Sparrow for one more go. I'd even say, get the fans to write in what they'd like to see happen."
Back in August, Pirates of the Caribbean producer Jerry Bruckheimer said he was now talking with Depp about his own potential return to the franchise, despite previous comments by the actor that made such a return seem extremely unlikely, as Disney mulled other, alternative routes forward for the franchise. Depp's past legal issues with ex-wife Amber Heard saw Disney largely distance itself from the star, leading to some choice words from Depp in response.
Long-gestating plans have placed Barbie star Margot Robbie at the forefront of Pirates 6 if and when it does ever materialize. That said, Bruckheimer has previously confirmed his intent that "some" previous Pirates of the Caribbean actors would return for the next movie, while also offering "a new take" on the franchise overall. Depp, meanwhile, appears to have retained a strong affection for his role as Jack Sparrow, which is widely seen as his most popular character among his fans. Fellow Pirates star Orlando Bloom has strongly hinted he wants to see Depp back, as well. Could Rush also follow? Get writing those letters.
Tom Phillips is IGN's News Editor. You can reach Tom at tom_phillips@ign.com or find him on Bluesky @tomphillipseg.bsky.social

item.title: Pokémon Pokopia has revealed what players can expect from its first Halloween-themed event, “Pumpkaboo’s Sweet Surprises.”
item.description:
Pokémon Pokopia has revealed what players can expect from its first Halloween-themed event, “Pumpkaboo’s Sweet Surprises.”
The limited-time event will run from 5am on October 17 until November 1, based on your Switch 2 system’s clock. (Looking at you, time travelers.) Pumpkaboo’s Sweet Surprises will follow a similar structure to previous events, featuring new Pokémon, decorations, and habitats, which require players to get their hands on a new currency: candy.
As the event’s title suggests, Pumpkaboo will be the star of Pokopia’s Halloween show. Starting on October 17, players will be able to start the event by talking to the dual-type Pokémon outside of finished Town Centers. Pumpkaboo will have plenty of new spooky items to trade, but he'll ask for some pumpkin candy in exchange.
We don't know the exact lineup of new items being added to the game, but promotional images show Jack-O-Lanterns, spooky trees, and a glowing ghost decoration.
How do you collect the candy to get these items? Well, players will need to have at least started the Bleak Beach area to get Zorua’s Camouflage ability. During the event, players will be able to use Camouflage to play tricks on their Pokémon, turning into their favorite items and then surprising them with their true Ditto form. Yep, your Pokémon will reward you for scaring and disappointing them.
Like previous events, some of the new Halloween-themed items can be used to build a new habitat. This time around, players can work toward building the habitat for Pumpkaboo’s evolution, Gourgeist. Both Pokémon will hang around after the event ends, giving players the chance to permanently add some spookier Ghost-types to their Pokopia areas.
We've had nothing but praise for Pokopia since it first launched, highlighting its "surprisingly deep world" in our original 9/10 review. With the cadence of updates, that world seems to just keep getting bigger. The previous in-game event, Fetching Scales for Feeba, was released soon after the massive 2.0 update and Bubbly Basin DLC.
Blythe (she/her) is an Audience Development Coordinator at IGN who spends way too much time in character customization screens and tracking down collectibles.

item.title: Diablo 5 game director Joe Shely has suggested a return to more methodical gameplay.
item.description:
Diablo 5 is still a couple of years away, but that hasn't stopped the speculation on how the game will actually play. People certainly expect a lot of elements from Diablo 3 and 4 to carry over to the new game, but Game Director Joe Shely has suggested a return to more methodical gameplay.
Seemingly in response to the video Path of Exile's Chris Wilson released about Diablo 5, Shely took to Twitter where he promised "while Diablo 5 will continue to feature some DEX (moment-to-moment execution) mechanics, on balance the game will be an INT/STR game (planning and investment)."
While Diablo V will continue to feature some DEX (moment-to-moment execution) mechanics, on balance the game will be an INT/STR game (planning and investment). We are designing to the core tenet of ARPGs that any challenge can be overcome with the right build.
There has been a lot of discussion around Blizzard invoking Diablo 2 when debuting Diablo 5 at Blizzcon, and how the team needs to shift away from the modern itemization and game design of the last few Diablo games to make that happen. According to Shely's post, it seems like Diablo 5 is heading in that direction. We'll just have to wait and see if Diablo 5's moment-to-moment gameplay is meaningfully different from Diablo 4's focus on infinitely scaling content that you clear in seconds. However, the community seems skeptical.
Over on Reddit, the top comment from user /u/Steve_Cage is simply "they said all this before 🤣🤣," and the top reply to that one is from /u/Tragedy_Boner who said, "They ALL say this. And when the game comes out most people want to blast and not be methodical. No modern ARPG ever stays slow." Some people seem to think that even if this is the goal from the start, Blizzard will reverse course after launch. User /u/Usernameasteriks says, "They won’t follow through, if they even try in the first place. Once the first wave of people complaining they can’t blast through content quickly they will restructure it all."
On Twitter, though, people seem a little more optimistic. User Dagon5 replied with, "I'm happy to hear this. Honestly this is an opportunity to try the other direction from what D3/D4 was trying to accomplish. Just go all in on itemization depth etc, and skill systems." And that certainly seems like what Shely is setting out to accomplilsh.
I've personally never had a problem with Diablo 4's approach to itemization, and I like jumping in and seeing just how far I can push in the Pit each season. But, I also jump back to Diablo and Diablo 2 occasionally when I want to play something that focuses more on creative itemization. Luckily, even if Diablo 5 does lean towards Diablo 2's way of doing things, it sounds like the team will keep adding new seasons to Diablo 4 after launch, so you can always just stick with that game.
Jackie Thomas is the Senior Tech Editor at IGN and the PC components queen. She's been covering gaming hardware for more than a decade for IGN, TechRadar, Gizmodo, PC Gamer and more. You can follow her @Jackiecobra

item.title: Peacock has officially announced Ted: The Animated Series, with Seth MacFarlane, Mark Wahlberg, and Amanda Seyfried returning to voice their original roles.
item.description:
Peacock announced Wednesday that TED: The Animated Series will premiere with eight episodes on December 17, with additional episodes set to stream in 2027.
Created by Seth MacFarlane, Paul Corrigan, and Brad Walsh, the cartoon is a sequel to the two live-action Ted movies. You can check out the teaser trailer here and find the new poster below.
The animated series brings back the cast of 2012’s Ted and 2015’s Ted 2.
MacFarlane reprises his role as the voice of Ted; Mark Wahlberg, as the voice of Ted's best friend, John; Amanda Seyfried, as the voice of John's wife, Sam; and Jessica Barth as Ted's wife, Tami-Lynn.
Kyle Mooney and Liz Richman also join the cast as series regulars in the roles of Apollo and Ruth, respectively.
“Picking up twelve years after the conclusion of the last movie, John and his thunder-buddy Ted are neighbors, both with families of their own and dead-end jobs,” according to the official plot synopsis.
“Follow these two lovable stoners as they enable each other's bad ideas about marriage, parenting and the challenges of adult life.”
Corrigan and Walsh serve as co-showrunners. Rough Draft Studios, Inc. animates the show.
McFarlane and Peacock previously teamed for two seasons of the live-action Ted: The TV Series.
McFarlane recently cast doubt on Peacock greenlighting Season 3 given the costly visual effects involved in bringing his foul-mouthed teddy bear character to life.

item.title: Former PlayStation boss Shawn Layden has offered new Xbox CEO some words of advice as she resets Microsoft’s gaming business: “pick a lane.”
item.description:
Former PlayStation boss Shawn Layden has offered new Xbox CEO some words of advice as she resets Microsoft’s gaming business: “pick a lane.”
In an interview with The Expansion Pass, the former boss of Sony Interactive Entertainment America called the decision Asha Sharma now faces Xbox’s “Dreamcast moment.”
This is a reference to Sega’s earth-shattering exit from the console business following the commercial failure of the Dreamcast. That call, made early 2001, ended a run of console manufacturing that included the likes of the Sega Genesis, Game Gear, and Sega Saturn. Sega instead focused on releasing video games on previously rival consoles, such as Sony's PS2.
Fast forward 25 years, and Xbox is in the middle of a dramatic restructure that has already seen nearly 2,000 staff lose their jobs, multiple studios either exit Xbox or face closure, and various games canceled. Xbox is now focused on fewer, bigger video game franchises such as The Elder Scrolls, Fallout, and Minecraft, with the likes of Halo moved over to Call of Duty company Activision. Through it all, there are question marks hanging over the viability of Xbox’s confirmed next-gen console, Project Helix.
With this in mind, Layden was asked if he had any advice for Sharma, having led a video game business of his own. He presented two options: go hard on taking on PlayStation now and in the future, with the assumed launch of Project Helix and PlayStation 6, or pack up those console plans and focus on software.
“You got to pick a lane,” he began. “Either you're going to be a platform competitive with PlayStation — which Xbox has not been competitive with PlayStation for years — but that's not out of the window. You know, you can still make another run at it. And there are certain decisions you have to make around that about the platform. We talked about exclusivity. We talked about, how do you incentivize third-parties to support your platform in a meaningful way? This is all things around the platform business.
“Or you sit back and realize you are the biggest game publisher in the world. Well maybe Tencent’s bigger, but in the Western world you are the biggest game publisher out there with Activision and Blizzard and Bethesda and all the other pieces. Be that. This is your Dreamcast moment, when Sega decided we're just going to be on PS2 and we're going to get out of the hardware business and just be a great software company. It can be done. It's been done before. So, that's my advice. Pick a lane.”
Microsoft has for years now fended off questions over whether it plans to exit the console hardware business amid poor sales of Xbox Series X and S and, before it, Xbox One. Publicly, Microsoft boss Satya Nadella and Asha Sharma have remained committed to console hardware, with Sharma saying it’s central to the company’s gaming plans. But Sharma has also said in recent months that Microsoft needs to think carefully about how Xbox consoles work and make money, particularly with the RAMpocalypse driving up prices.
In June, Sharma said the spiralling cost of new and existing consoles would require "radically different business models" over the coming generation. Speaking to Fortune, Sharma acknowledged the increasing price of existing hardware and components — fuelled by global crises and the rise of AI — and said the industry had "reached a point where it will be hard to imagine" mass audiences still being able to afford "thousands of dollars" for a new console generation.
And just this week, former PlayStation executive Shuhei Yoshida said Sony and Nintendo needed to make their current consoles last as long as possible amid soaring costs that have already prompted PS5 and Switch 2 price rises.
Big questions remain. What, exactly, does Project Helix look like? How far down the exclusivity road will Xbox go? And here’s the biggest of all: will Xbox eventually exit the console business?

item.title: Nintendo will launch a physical Switch 2 version of Pokémon Legends: Z-A with its Mega Dimension DLC bundled in.
item.description:
Nintendo will launch a physical Switch 2 version of Pokémon Legends: Z-A with its Mega Dimension DLC bundled in.
The complete version of the game will launch on cartridge this October 29, The Pokémon Company confirmed today. This will include the shinier version of the game playable on Nintendo Switch 2 (though this cartridge can also be played on Switch, if you want to buy now and upgrade your hardware later).
Mega Dimension is, of course, the expansion for Pokémon Legends: Z-A that allows players to go on further adventures in Lumiose City via new portals created by Hoopa. Key features here are the ability to temporarily control Pokémon at levels greater than 100, and encounter even more Mega Evolutions — such as Darkrai, Magearna and Baxcalibur.
While Mega Dimension launched last October as a separate download, this combined package means that anyone purchasing Pokémon Legends: Z-A this holiday will be able to get the complete game in one go. You'll also unlock a gift of 100 Ultra Balls to get your catching off to an ultra start.
Nintendo has no major new Pokémon game due this holiday, so a re-release of Pokémon Legends: Z-A makes sense. There's still some time to go until the next generation of Pokémon games arrives next year, exclusively for Switch 2, in the shape of Pokémon Winds and Pokémon Waves.
But could there be one other surprise before the end of the year? Some fans are convinced that re-releases of Pokémon Ruby, Sapphire and Emerald will also launch in 2026, though we'll have to wait and see if these become a reality.
"Pokémon Legends: Z-A finally feels like Game Freak hitting its stride in Pokémon's 3D era," IGN wrote in our Pokémon Legends Z-A review, awarding the game an 8/10 score. "Lumiose City may not be visually exciting, but exciting Pokémon encounters, well-written characters, and amusing side quests still make it fun to explore."
Tom Phillips is IGN's News Editor. You can reach Tom at tom_phillips@ign.com or find him on Bluesky @tomphillipseg.bsky.social

item.title: Marvel fans need to prepare for "a very surprising ending" to Avengers: Doomsday, directors Joe and Anthony Russo have teased.
item.description:
Marvel fans need to prepare for "a very surprising ending" to Avengers: Doomsday, directors Joe and Anthony Russo have teased.
Speaking to Fandango, Anthony Russo described the upcoming Marvel blockbuster as a "focused propulsive narrative," while still weighing in as one of the studio's longest films to date.
As you might expect from a movie with such a large cast, Avengers: Doomsday will clock in around the "two-and-half hour" mark, though even the Russos are unlikely to know the exact runtime just yet as reshoots were believed to be taking place only this month to add even more material.
Only three Marvel movies have ever stretched longer than two-and-a-half hours (150 minutes), with the appropriately named Eternals at an everlasting 157 minutes, Black Panther: Wakanda takes Forever at 161 minutes, and Avengers never Endgame at a whopping three hours and one minute (or 181 minutes total).
Still, Anthony Russo suggested Avengers: Doomsday audiences wouldn't be bored.
"It's a two-and-a-half hour movie or so, and you're sitting through it, and it's a focused propulsive narrative that has an organizing principle at its center, and everything has to orbit around that," he said. "That's part of the creative challenge for Joe and I — just figuring out what that orbit is and how it all smashes together."
As for how it all concludes — and leads into next year's climactic Avengers: Secret Wars — the Russo brothers had this to say:
"I think people are going to be surprised," Joe Russo teased. "It's a very surprising ending. It's a very surprising movie and that's all we'll say about it."
What could this mean? Well, with Doomsday being just part one of the story, it seems clear the movie will not end Doctor Doom's story just yet, and therefore it seems extremely unlikely the film will wrap everything up with a happy ending.
Even without knowledge of the Secret Wars comics or informed speculation based on filming leaks and reports, it seems fair to compare Doomsday to Infinity War, the first film in the Russo brothers' previous Avengers two-parter. That movie ended with the Avengers losing to Thanos, with multiple main character deaths throughout the film that were not reversed, then a climactic event that acted as a shocking cliffhanger. Will the Avengers lose again to Doctor Doom? I would not describe this as too surprising, but it would certainly serve as an interesting jumping off point for Secret Wars, should it follow the Marvel comics' general story.
The Russos have been doing the rounds promoting Avengers: Endgame Encore, which features four brand new scenes they have confirmed won't appear in Doomsday itself. One of these scenes sees Doom "collect" the Hulk, potentially suggesting he will sit out Doomsday and return in Secret Wars. Avengers: Doomsday launches in theaters on December 18.
